frames.commonConstraints:
Background: flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere, no checkerboard, no floor, no shadow. No text, lines, arrows, borders.
Layout: exactly two equal columns and two equal rows, overall square. One full-body frame per cell. Creature horizontally centered in each cell, feet baseline at 86% of the cell height, same body size in all four cells.
The four frames MUST look clearly different from each other (an animator's extreme keys). Keep both eyes visible in every frame. No human arms, no antenna, no screen face.
frames.record: The coding prompt is stored verbatim. The other four sheets were generated the same session with the same preamble and constraints; only their activity brief survives in the project record and is stored here as a summary, not as the literal prompt text.

prompts.prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve animation keyframes with LARGE pose differences. Edit target: the supplied reference sprite of MOSS, a squat terracotta clay box creature carrying a moss garden with a two-leaf sprout on its back, four short clay legs, two small dark eyes in a recessed face panel. Keep the exact same character, proportions, hand-painted pixel-art texture, warm palette, top-left light and outline weight as the reference.

Deliver a 2x2 keyframe sheet of this ONE character CODING on a big leaf keypad (a broad green leaf lying flat on the ground to the LEFT, with 6 pale stone keys on it; keypad about 60% of body width, clearly outside the body). A thick flexible brown root grows from Moss's left side as the typing limb.

Background: flat solid pure magenta #FF00FF everywhere, no checkerboard, no floor, no shadow. No text, lines, arrows, borders.
Layout: exactly two equal columns and two equal rows, overall square. One full-body frame per cell. Creature horizontally centered in each cell, feet baseline at 86% of the cell height, same body size in all four cells.

The four frames MUST look clearly different from each other (an animator's extreme keys):
Frame 1 (top-left): root limb raised HIGH above the keypad, higher than the eyes, curled like a question mark; body upright; eyes looking down at keys.
Frame 2 (top-right): root SLAMMED down onto a key; the body is squashed noticeably shorter and wider (about 12% shorter), eyes squeezed to happy arcs; the pressed key sunk; two little dust puffs of pollen rise from the key.
Frame 3 (bottom-left): root swung to the FAR right side of the keypad near the body, body stretched slightly taller and leaning left; the back leaves tilted left.
Frame 4 (bottom-right): root raised to mid height, body upright, eyes round, a glowing pale-yellow glyph square floating above the keypad (the typed character).

Keep both eyes visible in every frame. No human arms, no antenna, no screen face.

prompts.brief: READING a large leaf page held up in front of the body by a root; four keys of a page turn: leaf flat and open, leaf lifted at one corner, leaf mid-flip with eyes following it, leaf settled on the other side.

ERROR: the clay box has collapsed forward and sits low; a snapped brown root lies beside it; keys alternate between a slumped body with drooping leaves and a sharp jolt/jam with eyes pinched, no rising or recovery pose.
WAITING FOR THE USER: Moss raises one big leaf above its head and offers it toward the viewer; keys move from a low hold to a high stretched offer and back, eyes wide and looking out of the frame.
WAITING FOR A TOOL: an empty clay pot stands beside Moss; Moss leans to peer into it, leans back, tilts the other way and peers again, eyes tracking the pot.
